blocking.title: The new head guard misses a compare read at a descendant of pr.headSha: a head whose patch was never bound gets ready=true
blocking.failurePath: The S4 shell reads the PR at H1, which sets pr.headSha=H1 and changedFiles=3. The author pushes H2, a fast-forward that edits one line of an existing file, so the file count does not change. The shell then reads the compare by branch name, at H2: compare={files: H2's files, commits:[E, H1, H2]}. This is the "two reads across a push" case that the contract comment (lines 87-95) names. Checks read at H1 are green, and the build has verify, review and chief passes bound to D(H2). Line 279 only asks whether commits includes pr.headSha. H1 is an ancestor inside base..H2, so the guard does not fire and compare stays non-null. The digest is computed from H2's files; count-mismatch does not fire because the count is equal; the verdicts at D(H2) count, and the H1 evidence link counts too. Probe at the head (vitest in a scratch copy): {"ready":true,"headSha":"aaaa…(H1)","patchDigest":"pd2:da09…(D of H2)","blockers":[]}. So readiness reports H1 as ready even though no verdict was ever bound to H1's patch. S6a would stamp pacman/merge-gate success on H1, and the P4 executor would merge with sha=H1 if the branch tip is H1 at that moment, for example after a force-push back. That merges a patch nobody reviewed. The guard catches only the opposite direction, where the compare is older than the PR. The PR body ("never reports a head as ready from inputs read at another one"), its Acceptance item ("Inputs read at another head never give ready") and the squash message all claim the general property, and it does not hold. A related symptom of the same gap: when the push between the two reads changes the file count, the race shows up as count-mismatch, and line 289-290 classes it as compare-truncated, a human blocker. The contract says a cross-push read is the transient patch-unavailable.
blocking.evidence: readiness.ts:279-282: `if (compare !== null && pr !== null && !compare.commits.includes(pr.headSha)) { block('patch-unavailable', 'compare not read at the PR head'); compare = null; }`. Membership in base..head does not show that the compare's head is pr.headSha, because every ancestor commit of the PR is also in the list. readiness.ts:87-95 lists "跨推送的两次读" as a case this guard handles. The only test, merge-gate-readiness.test.ts:1124-1137, covers commits=[EARLIER], the older-compare direction. No test covers commits=[EARLIER, HEAD, NEWER]. Fix: add the SHA the shell requested, or the compare's own head, to the compare input (for example `compare.headSha`) and require it to equal pr.headSha. That covers both directions and keeps a cross-push race transient instead of letting it surface as count-mismatch (human).
skeptics:
Confirmed at c4bf400. In apps/server/src/services/merge-gate/readiness.ts, the head guard (lines 279-282) only checks `compare.commits.includes(pr.headSha)`. When the compare is read at H2, a descendant of pr.headSha=H1, H1 is in base..H2. The guard does not fire and compare stays non-null. The digest at lines 283-287 is then computed from H2's files, and count-mismatch only uses pr.changedFiles. Verdicts are matched by digest alone (lines 346-353). The evidence link only has to point at a commit in compare.commits, and H1 is one. Nothing else ties the compare's head to pr.headSha.

Probe: I extracted the head's merge-gate sources, shared package and readiness test into a scratch dir and ran vitest against them. I used the test's green() fixture with these changes:
- pr.headSha = HEAD (H1).
- compare = {files: H2 files (one file with a changed blob sha and patchSha, same count), commits: [EARLIER, HEAD, NEWER]}.
- verify, three reviews and chief, all passing at D(H2).

Result: {"ready":true,"headSha":"aaaa...(H1)","patchDigest":"pd2:3fa5a8...(D of H2)","blockers":[]}. So H1 is reported ready with H2's digest, and no verdict is bound to H1's patch.

Second probe: the same descendant compare with one extra file gives [["compare-truncated","human",["count-mismatch"]]]. A cross-push race therefore surfaces as a human blocker, not as the transient patch-unavailable the contract comment (lines 87-95) promises for "跨推送的两次读".

The only test of the guard (merge-gate-readiness.test.ts:1124-1137) covers commits=[EARLIER], the older-compare direction. The PR body and the member comment claim the general property: "never reports a head as ready from inputs read at another one" and "the result never names a head the inputs were not read at". That property does not hold for a compare read at a later head.

Confirmed at c4bf400. In apps/server/src/services/merge-gate/readiness.ts, line 279 is the only head guard: `if (compare !== null && pr !== null && !compare.commits.includes(pr.headSha))`. GateInputs.compare (line 96) is `{files, commits}` and carries no head SHA of its own, so the function cannot tell a compare read at pr.headSha apart from one read at a descendant of it. Every ancestor inside base..head is also in `commits`. For the scenario pr.headSha=H1, changedFiles=3, compare={files: H2's files with the same count, commits:[E, H1, H2]}, the guard does not fire. computePatchDigest then runs on H2's files, and count-mismatch does not fire because the counts are equal. The verdicts at D(H2) count, and so does a link at H1 to a file the PR changes. I ran a probe test in a scratch copy of the head tree (git archive, vitest 5.0.1) with exactly these inputs, and it passed with `ready === true`, `headSha === H1` and `patchDigest === D(H2)`, where D(H1) !== D(H2). So readiness reports H1 as ready under a digest that belongs to a different patch. The contract comment at lines 87-95 names "跨推送的两次读" (two reads across a push) as handled. The PR body says "never reports a head as ready from inputs read at another one", the Acceptance item says "Inputs read at another head never give ready", and the squash message makes the same claim, so all three state the general property. The only test (merge-gate-readiness.test.ts around line 1125) covers commits=[EARLIER], the older-compare direction. Whether S4 will read the compare by SHA instead of by branch is not set in this PR. The pure function's stated contract does not hold for the descendant case, so the finding stands.

blocking.title: The compare-at-head rule only catches a compare older than the PR head; a compare read at a newer head gives ready for the stale head (ticked acceptance item 8 is false in that direction, and no test covers it)
blocking.failurePath:
Input: `pr.headSha = EARLIER`, meaning the PR was read before a push, or from a stale cache. The compare was read after the push at the new head HEAD: `compare.commits = [EARLIER, HEAD]`, with HEAD's files. Verdicts are bound to that compare's digest D, and the checks are green.

`!compare.commits.includes(pr.headSha)` is false, because EARLIER is an earlier commit of the same PR. So no `patch-unavailable` is raised, and the digest, paths, evidence link and verdicts are all judged against HEAD's patch.

Result, run at head from a git-archive copy: `{ready: true, headSha: 'eeee…', patchDigest: 'pd2:81a5…', blockers: []}`. The function reports EARLIER as ready with the digest of a patch read at HEAD; EARLIER's own patch may differ and was never judged. Swapping in the opposite case (`pr.headSha = HEAD`, `commits = [EARLIER]`) gives `patch-unavailable`, which is the only direction tested.
blocking.evidence:
The ticked acceptance item says "Inputs read at another head never give ready". The round 8 text and the member comment say the rule means "the result never names a head the inputs were not read at". The `GateInputs.compare` comment (lines 87-95) motivates the rule with "cached responses, two reads across a push". A PR-then-compare read across a push yields exactly this reverse case.

The only test is at `merge-gate-readiness.test.ts:1124`: `commits = [EARLIER]`, head HEAD. A stricter rule would leave all 125 tests green, so the tests do not pin which direction the rule covers. Examples: the shell passes the SHA it requested the compare at and readiness checks it equals `pr.headSha`, or readiness requires the last element of `commits` to be the head.

There is no caller yet (S6a wires it). The concrete harm, once S4/S5 exist, is a `pacman/merge-gate` success written on a non-head SHA, and a ready result whose `headSha` and `patchDigest` describe different patches.

Fix: add the requested head SHA to the compare input and require it to equal `pr.headSha`. Add a test with `pr.headSha = EARLIER` and `commits = [EARLIER, HEAD]` expecting `patch-unavailable`.
skeptics:
Confirmed at c4bf4005060e8d86b998394d1a116b7a227e7e36. The finding is real.

The only check that ties the compare to the PR head is at readiness.ts:279: `!compare.commits.includes(pr.headSha)`. It asks only whether pr.headSha is one of the compare's commits. It never asks whether pr.headSha is the head the compare was read at. Nothing else in mergeReadiness looks at headSha; line 417 only copies it into the result.

If pr.headSha = EARLIER and compare.commits = [EARLIER, HEAD], the check passes. The compare is then used to judge everything that follows:
- the digest (line 286)
- the paths (line 300)
- the evidence link (lines 321-336), where any link at HEAD or EARLIER is accepted
- the verdicts at D (lines 346-397)

All of these describe HEAD's patch.

I reproduced it with vitest 5.0.1 on a git-archive copy of the PR head, using the test file's own green() fixture. I changed only `pr.headSha = EARLIER` and `commits = [EARLIER, HEAD]`. The result was `{"ready":true,"headSha":"eeee...","patchDigest":"pd2:81a5d0d5...","blockers":[]}`, which reports EARLIER as ready with the digest of HEAD's patch. The tested direction (`pr.headSha = HEAD`, `commits = [EARLIER]`) gives patch-unavailable "compare not read at the PR head", as expected. That is the only direction the test at merge-gate-readiness.test.ts:1124 covers.

The contract claims coverage that the code does not give:
- The GateInputs.compare comment (lines 87-95) gives "two reads across a push" as a reason for the rule. A PR read before a push followed by a compare read after it produces exactly this uncovered case.
- The PR body's round 8 text and the ticked Acceptance item "Inputs read at another head never give ready" both say the rule covers this.
- So does the member comment: "the result never names a head the inputs were not read at."

One mitigation I found, and why it is not enough: a count-mismatch blocker fires only when the two heads have different numbers of changed files. With equal counts, as in the reproduction, nothing catches it. The harm is latent, since there is no caller until S6a, and it depends on the S4 shell reading the compare by branch rather than by the exact SHA. The contract does not require reading by exact SHA.

I confirmed the failure at c4bf400. The only head-binding rule is in apps/server/src/services/merge-gate/readiness.ts:279: `if (compare !== null && pr !== null && !compare.commits.includes(pr.headSha))`. It checks only that the PR head appears somewhere in the compare's commit list. Nothing checks that the compare was read at that head, for example by requiring it to be the last commit or by comparing it against a requested-at SHA. So when the compare was read at a newer head and contains `pr.headSha` as an earlier commit, it is still accepted. The digest D (line 286), the path classes (line 300), the evidence-link set (lines 327-331) and the verdict filter `x.patchDigest === D` (line 351) then all judge the newer head's patch. The result is `headSha: pr.headSha` (line 417), which is the older head.

How I ran it: I extracted the PR head with git archive into a scratch directory, bundled it with esbuild (`@pacman/shared` resolved to the PR's own packages/shared), and used the test file's green() fixture. Results:
- Baseline (`pr.headSha=HEAD`, `commits=[EARLIER,HEAD]`): ready=true.
- Tested direction (`pr.headSha=HEAD`, `commits=[EARLIER]`): ready=false with patch-unavailable "compare not read at the PR head".
- Reverse direction (`pr.headSha=EARLIER`, `commits=[EARLIER,HEAD]`), with the evidence link at either HEAD or EARLIER: `{ready:true, headSha:'eeee...', patchDigest:'pd2:81a5d0d5...', blockers:[]}`. This is the reviewer's exact result.

Test coverage: in apps/server/test/merge-gate-readiness.test.ts, `pr.headSha` is never anything but HEAD. The commits overrides are only line 117 (`[EARLIER,HEAD]`), line 675 (`[HEAD]`) and line 1129 (`[EARLIER]` with head HEAD). No test covers the reverse case, and a stricter rule such as `commits.at(-1) === pr.headSha` would leave every existing test green.

Claims it contradicts:
- PR body round 8: "it never reports a head as ready from inputs read at another one".
- Ticked Acceptance item: "Inputs read at another head never give ready".
- Member comment: "the result never names a head the inputs were not read at".
- The `GateInputs.compare` comment (lines 87-95) gives "two reads across a push" as the motivation. When the PR is read first and the compare after a push, you get exactly this reverse case: checks and mergeable state taken at EARLIER, patch, digest and verdicts at HEAD, and a ready result naming EARLIER.

There is no caller yet (S4/S6a), so the harm is latent. The defect in the code and the false ticked acceptance claim are real at this head.

suggestions.title: Acceptance item 8 claims every input is bound to the head, but the checks input has no head, so check results from a previous head are accepted
suggestions.failurePath:
Scenario: an evidence-only push moves the head from H1 to H2. The digest is unchanged, so the verdicts stay valid. The shell's check list is still the one read at H1 (all green), and GitHub's asynchronous `mergeable_state` still says `clean`, which the comment at lines 237-241 says can happen.

Result: `mergeReadiness` returns ready for H2 while H2's required checks have not started. Nothing in `GateInputs.checks` lets the function notice, so the item is a contract on S4, not something this function or its tests can enforce.
suggestions.evidence:
`checks: {required, runs, statuses, complete}` has no head SHA; only the comment at lines 74-80 says "当前 head 的检查" ("checks on the current head"). The ticked item "Inputs read at another head never give ready" is backed in `s2-r8-red-green.txt` only by the compare test.

Fix: either narrow the wording to the compare, or add `checks.headSha` with a mismatch blocker and a row test.

suggestions.title: No test covers 'unstable' with unreadable checks; deleting that branch leaves all 125 tests green
suggestions.failurePath:
With `mergeableState = 'unstable'` and `checks = null` (or `complete: false`), the head returns `[['mergeable-state', 'unstable, checks unreadable'], ['required-checks-unreadable']]` (probe run).

Mutation: replace line 256 with a no-op for `notPassing === null`. The result drops to `['required-checks-unreadable']`, and every test still passes. No test combines unstable with unreadable checks: the only checks-null test (line 601) uses `clean`, and the incomplete-list test (line 928) also uses `clean`.

`ready` stays false, so this is only the PR's rule that every blocker is listed.
suggestions.evidence: A grep of the test file for `checks = null` and `complete = false` finds lines 603, 931 and 934, all with the baseline `mergeableState: 'clean'`. None of the mutation tables in `s2-mutations-8.txt` covers that branch.

suggestions.title: The head check accepts a compare read at a descendant or abandoned head, so readiness can report ready for pr.headSha using another patch's digest
suggestions.failurePath:
Line 279 only checks `compare.commits.includes(pr.headSha)`. That catches a compare read at an ancestor of the PR head, which is the case the test covers (the case at test line ~1124). It does not catch a compare read at a descendant of the head. Example: the PR read gives head H1; the compare was read when the branch tip was H2, a child of H1 (a cached response, or a branch later force-pushed back to H1). Then commits = [.., H1, H2] and the check passes. The digest, paths and verdict matching all run on H2's files. If H2 touches the same file set, pr.changedFiles still matches and count-mismatch does not fire. The function then returns ready:true with headSha H1 (line 417) and patchDigest D(H2), so H2's verify/review/decision verdicts are applied to H1's patch. Probe: I ran the head's readiness.ts in a scratchpad with pr.headSha=H1, compare.commits=[H0,H1,H2], H2's files and verdicts at D(H2). The result was {ready:true, headSha:H1, patchDigest:D(H2), blockers:[]}.

This is a suggestion, not a blocking finding:
- Nothing calls mergeReadiness at this head.
- On a forward push, GitHub's merge `sha` guard would refuse a merge at H1.
- Only the force-push-back case gets past the sha guard, and D3 also requires P4 to recompute the digest at merge time.

The PR body says readiness 'never reports a head as ready from inputs read at another one', which overstates what the check does. Suggested fix: have S4 pass the head sha the compare was requested at, and require it to equal pr.headSha, or require the compare's head commit to be pr.headSha. Either is stronger than set membership. Pin the descendant case with a test.
suggestions.evidence: readiness.ts:279 `if (compare !== null && pr !== null && !compare.commits.includes(pr.headSha))`; readiness.ts:417 `headSha: pr?.headSha ?? null`; readiness.ts:286-287 digest from compare.files. Scratchpad probe output: {"ready":true,"headSha":"aaaa…","patchDigest":"pd2:86eb…","digestOfH2Files":"pd2:86eb…","blockers":[]}
